```{r}
table_2_4 <- tibble::tribble(~fuel, ~`Table 2.4 row`,
  41.0, "All boreal forest", 50.4, "All other temperate forests", 3.3, "Savanna woodland, mid or late dry season burns",
  4.1, "Grassland, mid or late dry season burns", 14.3, "All shrublands", 26.7, "Shrubland (general)")
table_2_5 <- tibble::tribble(~ef_row, ~co2, ~ch4, ~n2o,
  "Savanna and grassland", 1613, 2.3, 0.21, "Extra tropical forest", 1569, 4.7, 0.26)
used <- fires |>
  dplyr::filter(source == "FAO TIER 1", year >= 2001, item %in% c("Other forest", "Woody savanna", "Savanna", "Grassland", "Open shrubland", "Closed shrubland")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(element = dplyr::case_match(element, "Burned Area" ~ "ha", "Emissions (CO2)" ~ "co2", "Emissions (CH4)" ~ "ch4", "Emissions (N2O)" ~ "n2o", .default = "dm")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(item, year), names_from = element, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::filter(ha > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fuel = dm / ha, dplyr::across(c(co2, ch4, n2o), \(x) x * 1e6 / dm))
coefficients <- used |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = item, `Burned area (kha a year)` = round(sum(ha) / 24 / 1000), fuel_min = min(fuel), fuel_max = max(fuel),
                   `CO2 (g/kg)` = round(mean(co2)), `CH4 (g/kg)` = round(mean(ch4), 2), `N2O (g/kg)` = round(mean(n2o), 2)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Fuel (t/ha)` = dplyr::if_else(round(fuel_min, 1) == round(fuel_max, 1), sprintf("%.1f", fuel_min), sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", fuel_min, fuel_max)),
                `Table 2.4 row` = dplyr::coalesce(table_2_4$`Table 2.4 row`[match(round(fuel_min, 1), table_2_4$fuel)], paste(table_2_4$`Table 2.4 row`[1:2], collapse = " to ")),
                `CO2 (g/kg)` = dplyr::if_else(is.na(`CO2 (g/kg)`), "not reported", format(`CO2 (g/kg)`, big.mark = ",")),
                `Table 2.5 row` = table_2_5$ef_row[match(`CH4 (g/kg)`, table_2_5$ch4)]) |>
  dplyr::select(Item = item, `Burned area (kha a year)`, `Fuel (t/ha)`, `Table 2.4 row`, `CO2 (g/kg)`, `CH4 (g/kg)`, `N2O (g/kg)`, `Table 2.5 row`)

trees_uncertainty <- function(ci_half_width) 0.524417 / 1.645006 * ci_half_width

buffer_table <- c(none = 0.25, `1` = 0.20, `2` = 0.15, `3` = 0.20,
                  `1,2` = 0.10, `1,3` = 0.15, `2,3` = 0.10, `1,2,3` = 0.05)

trees_buffer <- function(mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  buffer_table[[mitigating]] + if (after_reversal) 0.05 else 0
}

kept <- function(ci_half_width, mitigating = "none", after_reversal = FALSE) {
  1 - trees_uncertainty(ci_half_width) - trees_buffer(mitigating, after_reversal)
}

break_even <- function(...) (1 - trees_buffer(...)) / (0.524417 / 1.645006)

crediting_level <- function(x, years) sum(x[years]) / 5

accounts <- national |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 2012) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reference = year <= 2016)

level_split  <- sum(accounts$human[accounts$reference]) / 5
level_whole  <- sum(accounts$net[accounts$reference]) / 5

credits <- accounts |>
  dplyr::filter(!reference) |>
  dplyr::transmute(Year = year,
                   `Disaggregated emissions (Mt)` = human,
                   `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_split - human, 1),
                   `Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)` = net,
                   `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(level_whole - net, 1))

split_pos <- credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
whole_pos <- credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
worst <- which.min(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

bc_split_pos <- bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_whole_pos <- bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]] > 0
bc_worst <- which.min(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]])

classify <- function(n) {
  base <- forest_co2[forest_co2$year < min(forest_co2$year) + n, ]
  thr <- mean(base$co2) + 2 * stats::sd(base$co2)
  data.frame(`Baseline (years)` = n,
             Period = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_character_ else
               paste(min(base$year), max(base$year), sep = "-"),
             `Threshold (kt)` = if (nrow(base) < n) NA_real_ else round(thr),
             `Years classified natural` = if (nrow(base) < n) "baseline longer than the series" else
               paste(forest_co2$year[forest_co2$co2 > thr], collapse = ", "),
             check.names = FALSE)
}
baselines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(13, 20, 30), classify))

ci <- c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.50, 2.00)
deductions <- data.frame(
  `Uncertainty, 90% interval half width (%)` = ci * 100,
  `Uncertainty deduction (%)` = round(100 * trees_uncertainty(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 25% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci), 1),
  `Kept, 5% buffer (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, "1,2,3"), 1),
  `Kept, 30% buffer after a reversal (%)` = round(100 * kept(ci, after_reversal = TRUE), 1),
  check.names = FALSE)

set.seed(42)
sd_mt <- 16.6 * (44 / 12) / 1.96

simulate_reductions <- function(reference, emissions, n = 10000) {
  level <- rowMeans(matrix(rep(reference, each = n) +
                             stats::rnorm(n * length(reference), 0, sd_mt), nrow = n))
  level - (emissions + stats::rnorm(n, 0, sd_mt))
}

monte_carlo <- function(reference, series) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(series)), function(k) {
    draws <- simulate_reductions(reference, series$emissions[k])
    half <- (stats::quantile(draws, 0.95) - stats::quantile(draws, 0.05)) / 2
    data.frame(Year = series$year[k], mean = mean(draws), half = half,
               ci = half / abs(mean(draws)))
  }))
}

reference_split <- accounts$human[accounts$reference]
reference_whole <- accounts$net[accounts$reference]

mc_split <- monte_carlo(reference_split,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Disaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))
mc_whole <- monte_carlo(reference_whole,
  data.frame(year = credits$Year, emissions = credits[["Undisaggregated emissions (Mt)"]]))

blank_if_negative <- function(value, mean_reduction) ifelse(mean_reduction > 0, value, NA)

uncertainty <- data.frame(
  Year = mc_split$Year,
  `Disaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_split$mean, 1),
  `Disaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_split$ci), mc_split$mean),
  `Disaggregated deduction (%)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * trees_uncertainty(mc_split$ci), 1), mc_split$mean),
  `Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)` = round(mc_whole$mean, 1),
  `Undisaggregated interval (% of mean)` = blank_if_negative(round(100 * mc_whole$ci), mc_whole$mean),
  check.names = FALSE)

over <- uncertainty[["Disaggregated deduction (%)"]] > 100
banked <- ifelse(mc_split$mean > 0, 100 * purrr::map2_dbl(mc_split$ci, mc_split$Year > min(credits$Year[!split_pos]), \(ci, after) kept(ci, after_reversal = after)), NA)

msd <- \(x) sprintf("%.1f ± %.1f Mt CO~2~e a year (95 per cent confidence interval %.1f to %.1f)",
                    mean(x), stats::sd(x), stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[1], stats::t.test(x)$conf.int[2])
province <- dplyr::filter(eccc, region == "BC")
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

Separating natural disturbance from human activity, as the 2019 Refinement to the guidelines of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change allowed, decided whether Canada and British Columbia had any forest carbon credit to claim in the large fire years of 2017 to 2024. Few studies have run a national inventory through a crediting standard with and without that separation, and the guidance set no length for the record behind it. This study compared the two accounts for Canada and British Columbia using the 2026 national inventory (1990 to 2024) and applied the crediting level, Monte Carlo uncertainty deduction and buffer of the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard to 2017 to 2024. It also tested baselines of 13, 20 and 30 years for classing a fire year as natural, and recovered the coefficients behind the fire emissions that the Food and Agriculture Organization published for Canada. The account Canada reported showed reductions in `r sum(split_pos)` of `r nrow(credits)` crediting years, totalling `r round(sum(credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][split_pos]), 1)` million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, while the same land without the separation showed them in `r sum(whole_pos)` years and fell `r format(abs(credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][worst]), big.mark = ",")` million tonnes short in `r credits$Year[worst]` alone. British Columbia showed `r round(sum(bc_credits[["Disaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_split_pos]), 1)` million tonnes of reductions separated and fell `r format(abs(bc_credits[["Undisaggregated reductions (Mt)"]][bc_worst]), big.mark = ",")` million tonnes short without it. Lengthening the baseline from 13 to 20 years raised the natural disturbance threshold by `r round(100 * (baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][2] / baselines[["Threshold (kt)"]][1] - 1))` per cent without changing the years it marked, and the two deductions left nothing to issue once uncertainty reached `r round(100 * break_even())` per cent. The Food and Agriculture Organization applied savanna and grassland emission factors to Canadian forest fires, putting their methane at `r round(100 * table_2_5$ch4[1] / table_2_5$ch4[2])` per cent of its cited method. It also classed `r round(100 * sum(savanna_share[["Savanna fires"]]) / sum(savanna_share[["Savanna fires"]] + savanna_share[["Forest fires"]]))` per cent of the burned area as savanna, grassland or shrubland, for which it reported no carbon dioxide. Crediting standards that relied on the separation therefore needed a stated record length, a stated regrowth period and an uncertainty deduction taken on gross rather than net fluxes.

# Introduction

National greenhouse gas inventories reported the land sector on the assumption that every emission and removal on managed land was caused by people [@kurz2018quantifying], a convention the 2019 Refinement to the IPCC Guidelines called the managed land proxy, abbreviated there as MLP. In Canada's managed forest the convention joined harvest and regrowth to fire and insects, whose emissions and later removals were large and varied widely between years, and so masked the effect of management on the reported trend [@kurz2018quantifying]. The Refinement used Canada's series for 1990 to 2016 as its example of year-to-year variation from natural disturbance much larger than that of the rest of the managed forest [@ogle2019generic]. It offered "an approach that countries can apply on a voluntary basis within the MLP in order to indicate those emissions and removals considered to result from human activity, and those that are understood to result from natural disturbances" [@ogle2019generic]. The approach assumed that the carbon dioxide released would "be balanced by subsequent removals across the landscape at some future point in time" [@ogle2019generic].

The effect of the convention in Canada was known before the Refinement. With random future fire and insect outbreaks included, the Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector projected the managed forest as a source of 30 to 245 Mt CO~2~e a year in 2008 to 2012, the first commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol [@kurz2008risk]. That range equalled nearly 30 per cent of Canada's emissions in 2005, and natural disturbance was among the reasons Canada did not elect forest management under the Protocol [@kurz2008risk]. A forecast to 2100 put the annual chance of a sink after 2050 near 70 per cent if area burned stayed at its late twentieth-century level and 35 per cent if it rose [@metsaranta2010implications]. Canada's 2017 inventory then split the managed forest into land dominated by natural disturbance and the remaining managed forest, two components that summed to the net flux of the whole [@kurz2018quantifying]. A burned stand stayed in the natural part until it had grown back to the age at which it had enough wood to be worth cutting, 60 years nationally in 2017 [@kurz2018quantifying] and later 60 to 100 years by region [@kurz2024revised]. A revised harvest record for 1889 to 1989 moved 34 million hectares out of the managed part and cut the human sink reported for 1990 by 113 Mt CO~2~e, or 56 per cent, without any change in the forest [@kurz2024revised]. Read from the same inventory tables, forestry was a net source of 90.8 Mt CO~2~e a year over 2005 to 2021 against a reported sink of 4.7 Mt, a difference the authors explained by the treatment of wildfire as natural [@bysouth2024high].

Other countries separated the same fluxes by other routes, the United States by dividing forest carbon change among growth, land use change and natural disturbances such as fire [@woodall2015forest]. Australia classed a whole fire season as natural when national fire emissions exceeded the mean of a 2000 to 2012 baseline by two standard deviations and a state's burned area exceeded its own mean by one [@bowman2023wildfire]. The choice of route mattered more as disturbance rose. European forest carbon uptake in 2020 to 2023 was 17 to 27 per cent below its 1990 to 2019 average in every dataset compared [@linscheid2026forest]. A preprint projected a 44 per cent fall in the forest sink of the European Union by 2030 [@ritter2025alarming]. In North America in 2010 to 2019 the inventories reported a net source of 7,270 Tg CO~2~e a year, against 6,132 Tg from atmospheric inversions and 9,060 Tg from process models, a gap partly due to what each counted as human [@poulter2026north]. Countries together reported a net land sink of 1.6 Gt CO~2~ a year over 2000 to 2020, where FAOSTAT estimated a net source of 1.1 Gt [@grassi2022carbon].

In the Kyoto period, before the Refinement, factoring out natural and indirect human effects was already treated as a requirement of accounting that tied credits clearly to human activity, and @canadell2007factoring set out five ways to do it. These were longer accounting periods to reduce the effect of year-to-year variation, correction of inventories for that variation, activity-based accounting with carbon response curves, national baselines, and stratification of the landscape by average carbon stock. A review of the rules from Kyoto to Paris concluded that "factoring out direct human-induced from indirect human-induced and natural impacts on managed lands" was among the requirements "not sufficiently secured by currently discussed accounting rules" [@krug2018accounting]. The forest reference levels of the European Union were also shown to have credited harvest increases that policy assumed and that never took place [@grassi2018science].

Canada's reported figures came from one model, the Carbon Budget Model of the Canadian Forest Sector (CBM-CFS3), the core of a national reporting system that used a Tier 3 method built on the gain and loss approach of the IPCC [@kurz2018quantifying]. The model grew each stand along an empirical yield curve, reset its age to zero after a stand-replacing disturbance, and moved its carbon among pools, to the air and to forest products through a disturbance matrix for each type of disturbance [@kurz2018quantifying]. Over 71 years of reconstructed growth on a boreal landscape in eastern Canada it underestimated the net biomass gain of undisturbed stands by 10 per cent [@bernier2010reconstructing]. Its fire matrices assumed that every fire burned at high severity, and a sub-model built on mapped burn severity gave regional emissions typically 10 to 25 per cent lower than the existing approach [@thompson2026incorporating]. Applied to 26 countries of the European Union for 2000 to 2012, the same model matched the inventories well in nine and partly in ten, and the mismatches arose from how year-to-year variation and the carbon dioxide from fire were represented [@pilli2016modellinga].

Whether a fire year counted as natural depended on the statistics of the fire regime, a field older than any inventory. Under random fire the expected distribution of stand ages was the negative exponential, so that "the present age-class structure of such a forest is the key to its past fire history" [@wagner1978class]. The negative exponential and Weibull models became the standard descriptions of fire history [@johnson1985theory], with the fire cycle defined as the time taken to burn an area equal to the area studied [@johnson1991climatically]. Fire cycles reported for Canada ran from 50 years before 1730 and 90 years after it in the Kananaskis watershed of Alberta [@johnson1991climatically] to 229 years in eastern Canada [@cyr2016quantifying], 247 years in central Quebec [@belisle2011fire] and 769 years in Newfoundland [@arsenault2016unravelling]. The estimates depended on the record behind them, since lengthening a Landsat series in Portugal from 22 to 31 years substantially changed the fitted Weibull parameters [@oliveira2011fire] and short-term variation in fire activity degraded parametric estimates of the fire cycle [@cyr2016quantifying]. A censored tail of old stands could also falsely suggest that fire frequency had changed [@finney1995missing]. A normal fire year was defined, by analogy with climate normals, from 26-year means around Yosemite [@lutz2011fire], while charcoal records spanning millennia were proposed as the baseline wherever recent fires were too few [@gavin2007forest].

The uncertainty of a reported balance was bounded by the method that combined it. Approach 1 of the 2019 Refinement "theoretically requires that the standard deviation divided by the mean value is less than 0.3", and Monte Carlo simulation, Approach 2, "will be particularly appropriate to use when uncertainties are large, their distribution are non-Gaussian, and algorithms are complex functions" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. Neither prevented an uncertainty larger than the estimate, because a percentage uncertainty was the interval divided by the reported value. The guidance itself advised caution "in cases where the point estimate is very small when compared with the size of the confidence interval (e.g. a sector or inventory where removals and emissions are of similar sizes)" [@paciornik2019uncertainties]. Regional carbon budgets met the same limit, Australia's land taking up 36 ± 29 Tg C a year over 1990 to 2011 [@haverd2013australian] and the Brazilian Amazon giving −59 ± 160 Tg C a year from bottom-up estimates over 2010 to 2018 [@rosan2023contemporary]. The interval of Canada's own model was 32.2 Tg C a year wide, which @metsaranta2017uncertainty stated "cannot be meaningfully expressed in percentage terms because its range of possible values contains zero".

The fire emissions a government reached for first were those of FAOSTAT, which the IPCC recommended for checking the activity data and emission estimates of an inventory. Its Emissions from Fires domain covered every country for 1990 to 2024. The methodological note gave the equation, burned biomass multiplied by a default emission factor, and named the inputs, the MODIS MCD64A1 burned area product, the MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover product and the defaults of the 2006 IPCC Guidelines [@fao2025fires]. The note did not give the code run in Google Earth Engine, the rule that allocated a fuel value to each pixel, or the meaning of keeping "only those pixels with a percentage uncertainty lower than 20 percent" [@fao2025fires]. It also set the emissions of fires in organic soils to zero outside Southeast Asia, publishing the full values in a separate table [@fao2025fires]. Independent estimates of fire emissions disagreed widely, four satellite burned area datasets for Siberia differing up to fivefold [@kukavskaya2013fire] and the fires of 2022 in France emitting twice the estimate of the Global Fire Assimilation System once soil smouldering was counted [@vallet2025soil]. The IPCC Tier 1 defaults themselves gave global results that differed by about 40 per cent between the guidance of 2003 and that of 2006 [@petrescu2012global].

What the separation was worth was set by the crediting standard. The REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard stated that "only anthropogenic emissions shall be considered, and IPCC guidance shall be adhered to on any exclusion of non-anthropogenic emissions", and its 2025 draft added that natural disturbances "may be excluded if they are 'non-anthropogenic events or non-anthropogenic circumstances that cause significant emissions and are beyond the control of, and not materially influenced by a country'" [@art2021trees; @art2025trees3; @ogle2019generic]. Two deductions then scaled off the reported account. The uncertainty deduction multiplied gross reductions and removals by an adjustment factor, 0.524417 divided by 1.645006 times the half width of the 90 per cent confidence interval from 10,000 Monte Carlo iterations [@art2021trees]. The buffer withheld 25 per cent of the same quantity, 5 per cent where three mitigating factors were met, plus 5 percentage points for five years after a reversal [@art2021trees]. The Forest Carbon Partnership Facility instead set aside 10 to 40 per cent against reversal, of which exposure to fire, storms and drought contributed 0, 3 or 5 points, and it capped its uncertainty set-aside at 15 per cent for any uncertainty above 100 per cent [@fcpf2024buffer]. Verra scored each project's buffer from a risk rating with a minimum of 12 per cent, assessing natural risk from the events of the last 100 years and extrapolating where data covered at least 20 [@verra2024nprt]. A preprint put the chance of a reversal within 100 years at 31 to 42 per cent worldwide, highest in North American conifer forests among others, and observed that most buffer pools did not vary through space [@wu2026global].

None of the works this review charted ran a jurisdiction's account through a crediting standard both with and without the separation. The nearest compared Canada's reported series under different partitions [@kurz2024revised; @bysouth2024high], compared national inventories with independent estimates [@pilli2016modellinga; @grassi2022carbon], or mapped reversal risk without reference to an inventory [@wu2026global]. This study therefore aimed to test the natural disturbance approach introduced in the 2019 Refinement by comparing what Canada and British Columbia reported, and what they could have been credited, with and without it over 1990 to 2024, the period of the 2026 national inventory. It also aimed to test whether the fire emissions FAOSTAT published could be rebuilt from its stated method and the IPCC Tier 1 steps it cited, and it pursued three objectives.

1. To compare the net emissions of the two accounts for 1990 to 2024, and the reductions, the uncertainty estimated by the Monte Carlo approach of the 2019 Refinement and the buffer of each, under the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard for 2017 to 2024.
2. To test how a baseline of 13, 20 or 30 years, a length the 2019 Refinement left unstated, changed the threshold and the years classed as natural, and to show where the regrowth period and a net near zero made the separation hard to apply.
3. To rebuild the forest fire emissions FAOSTAT published for Canada from its stated method and the IPCC Tier 1 steps it cited, and to compare them with what Canada reported.

# Materials and Methods

## Literature review

A scoping review mapped the literature behind the Introduction and the Discussion, following the five stages of @arksey2005scoping as refined by @levac2010scoping and @peters2020updated, and was reported against the extension of the PRISMA checklist for scoping reviews [@tricco2018prisma]. The review questions, the search strings and the rules for what would change each claim were committed in a protocol before the first query ran. Search terms were drawn only from the title, subtitle and keywords the manuscript had on 22 October 2026, and each search wrote its results to a file that later renders read in place of the services.

```{r}
#| label: review-terms
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("04.references/review/search-terms.csv")) {
  front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
  small <- c("a", "an", "and", "as", "at", "by", "do", "does", "for", "from", "how", "in", "into", "is", "its", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "under", "using", "versus", "what", "why", "with")
  phrases <- \(x) x |>
    stringr::str_to_lower() |>
    stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]-]", " | ") |>
    stringr::str_replace_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(small, collapse = "|"), ")\\b"), " | ") |>
    stringr::str_split_1("\\|") |>
    stringr::str_squish() |>
    purrr::keep(\(p) nchar(p) > 2)
  dir.create("04.references/review", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(term = stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(unlist(front$keywords))), source = "keywords"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$title), source = "title"),
    tibble::tibble(term = phrases(front$subtitle %||% ""), source = "subtitle")
  ) |>
    dplyr::distinct(term, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(question = NA, concept = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("04.references/review/search-terms.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-queries
#| echo: true

front <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE))
declared <- paste(front$title, front$subtitle, paste(unlist(front$keywords), collapse = " ")) |>
  stringr::str_remove_all("[*_]") |>
  stringr::str_to_lower()
term_regex <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"))) else paste0("\\b", stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
terms <- readr::read_csv("04.references/review/search-terms.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(question), !is.na(concept)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(term = stringr::str_to_lower(term)) |>
  tidyr::separate_longer_delim(question, " ")
stray <- terms$term[!purrr::map_lgl(terms$term, \(x) stringr::str_detect(declared, term_regex(x)))]
if (nrow(terms) == 0) stop("No search terms selected in 04.references/review/search-terms.csv")
if (length(stray) > 0) stop("Not in the title, subtitle or keywords: ", paste(unique(stray), collapse = ", "))
queries <- terms |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(question, concept), group = paste(term, collapse = "|")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = question, route = paste(c(dplyr::first(question), concept), collapse = "-"), concepts = paste(group, collapse = " AND "))
record_id <- \(doi, title) dplyr::coalesce(stringr::str_to_lower(doi), stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[^[:alnum:] ]", " "))))
```

```{r}
#| label: review-store
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")) {
  dir.create("02.inputs/derived", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  # library-science manifest, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/blob/main/library/manifest.csv
  manifest <- readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  # library-science source notes, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/tree/main/sources
  notes <- tibble::tibble(path = list.files("../library-science/sources", "\\.md$", full.names = TRUE)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(key = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)), note = purrr::map_chr(path, \(p) paste(readLines(p, warn = FALSE), collapse = " ")))
  store <- manifest |>
    dplyr::filter(status %in% c("verified", "filed", "unverified"), !is.na(title) | !is.na(key)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(notes, key, note), by = "key") |>
    dplyr::mutate(text = stringr::str_to_lower(paste(title, note)))
  hits <- queries |>
    purrr::pmap(\(question, route, concepts) {
      groups <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ")
      term <- \(x) if (stringr::str_ends(x, "\\*")) paste0(stringr::str_escape(stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$")), "\\w*") else paste0(stringr::str_escape(x), "\\b")
      patterns <- purrr::map_chr(groups, \(g) paste0("\\b(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), term), collapse = "|"), ")"))
      keep <- purrr::map(patterns, \(r) stringr::str_detect(store$text, r)) |> purrr::reduce(`&`)
      store[keep, ] |> dplyr::transmute(question, route = paste0("store-", route), key, doi, title, year, venue = container, source_note = dplyr::if_else(has_source_note == "yes", key, NA))
    }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  readr::write_csv(hits, "02.inputs/derived/review-store-hits.csv")
  queries |>
    dplyr::transmute(strand = "library-science", route = paste0("store-", route), query = concepts, date = as.character(Sys.Date())) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::count(hits, route, name = "retrieved"), by = "route") |>
    dplyr::mutate(retrieved = tidyr::replace_na(retrieved, 0L), reported_total = retrieved, cap = NA, capped = FALSE, error = NA) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-log-store.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-openalex
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv")) {
  search_openalex <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 2000) {
    query <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ") |>
      purrr::map_chr(\(g) paste0("(", paste0('"', stringr::str_remove(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), "\\*$"), '"', collapse = " OR "), ")")) |>
      paste(collapse = " AND ")
    tryCatch({
      works <- list(); page <- 1; total <- NA
      repeat {
        # OpenAlex works, searched on title and abstract, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
        body <- httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
          httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title_and_abstract.search:", query), `per-page` = 200, page = page,
                               select = "doi,title,publication_year,primary_location,type,cited_by_count,abstract_inverted_index") |>
          httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 8, is_transient = \(r) httr2::resp_status(r) == 429, backoff = \(i) 15 * i) |>
          httr2::req_perform() |>
          httr2::resp_body_json()
        total <- body$meta$count
        works <- c(works, body$results)
        Sys.sleep(3)
        if (length(body$results) < 200 || length(works) >= min(total, cap)) break
        page <- page + 1
      }
      hits <- works |>
        purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = stringr::str_remove(w$doi %||% NA_character_, "^https://doi.org/"), title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$publication_year %||% NA_integer_,
                                       venue = w$primary_location$source$display_name %||% NA_character_, type = w$type %||% NA_character_, citations = w$cited_by_count %||% NA_integer_,
                                       abstract = if (length(w$abstract_inverted_index) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(rep(names(w$abstract_inverted_index), lengths(w$abstract_inverted_index))[order(unlist(w$abstract_inverted_index))], collapse = " "))) |>
        purrr::list_rbind() |>
        dplyr::mutate(question, route = paste0("oa-", route), .before = 1)
      list(hits = hits, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(hits), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA))
    }, error = \(e) list(hits = NULL, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "openalex", route = paste0("oa-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = 0L, reported_total = NA, cap, capped = FALSE, error = conditionMessage(e))))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_openalex)
  hits <- purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind()
  dir.create("02.inputs/review/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  hits |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = record_id(doi, title), abstract) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/review/raw/review-abstracts.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(dplyr::select(hits, -abstract), "02.inputs/derived/review-openalex-hits.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), "02.inputs/derived/review-log-openalex.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-semantic-scholar
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv")) {
  search_s2 <- function(question, route, concepts, cap = 3000) {
    query <- stringr::str_split_1(concepts, " AND ") |>
      purrr::map_chr(\(g) paste0("(", paste(purrr::map_chr(stringr::str_split_1(g, "\\|"), \(x) if (grepl(" ", x)) paste0('"', stringr::str_remove(x, "\\*$"), '"') else x), collapse = " | "), ")")) |>
      paste(collapse = " + ")
    tryCatch({
      papers <- list(); token <- NULL; total <- NA
      repeat {
        # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph bulk search, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data/operation/get_graph_paper_bulk_search
        body <- httr2::request("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search/bulk") |>
          httr2::req_url_query(query = query, fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds,citationCount,publicationTypes", token = token) |>
          httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
          httr2::req_perform() |>
          httr2::resp_body_json()
        total <- body$total; token <- body$token
        papers <- c(papers, body$data)
        if (is.null(token) || length(papers) >= cap) break
      }
      works <- papers |>
        purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w$title %||% NA_character_, year = w$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w$venue %||% NA_character_, type = paste(unlist(w$publicationTypes), collapse = " "), citations = w$citationCount %||% NA_integer_)) |>
        purrr::list_rbind()
      list(hits = dplyr::mutate(works, question, route = paste0("s2-", route), .before = 1),
           log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = nrow(works), reported_total = total, cap, capped = total > cap, error = NA))
    }, error = \(e) list(hits = NULL, log = tibble::tibble(strand = "semantic-scholar", route = paste0("s2-", route), query, date = as.character(Sys.Date()), retrieved = 0L, reported_total = NA, cap, capped = FALSE, error = conditionMessage(e))))
  }
  runs <- purrr::pmap(queries, search_s2)
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "hits") |> purrr::list_rbind() |> dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(question = character(), route = character(), doi = character(), title = character())), "02.inputs/derived/review-s2-hits.csv", na = "")
  readr::write_csv(purrr::map(runs, "log") |> purrr::list_rbind(), "02.inputs/derived/review-log-s2.csv", na = "")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-chase
#| echo: true

central <- c()
if (length(central) > 0 && !file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")) {
  chase <- function(seed_doi, direction) {
    # Semantic Scholar Academic Graph references and citations, https://api.semanticscholar.org/api-docs/graph#tag/Paper-Data
    resp <- httr2::request(paste0("https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/DOI:", seed_doi, "/", direction)) |>
      httr2::req_url_query(fields = "title,year,venue,externalIds", limit = 1000) |>
      httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 6) |>
      httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
      httr2::req_perform()
    if (httr2::resp_status(resp) != 200) return(tibble::tibble(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), error = httr2::resp_status_desc(resp)))
    key <- if (direction == "references") "citedPaper" else "citingPaper"
    httr2::resp_body_json(resp)$data |>
      purrr::map(\(w) tibble::tibble(doi = w[[key]]$externalIds$DOI %||% NA_character_, title = w[[key]]$title %||% NA_character_, year = w[[key]]$year %||% NA_integer_, venue = w[[key]]$venue %||% NA_character_)) |>
      purrr::list_rbind() |>
      dplyr::mutate(seed = seed_doi, route = paste0("chase-", direction), .before = 1)
  }
  tidyr::expand_grid(seed_doi = central, direction = c("references", "citations")) |>
    purrr::pmap(chase) |>
    purrr::list_rbind() |>
    readr::write_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-chase-hits.csv")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: review-screening
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv")) {
  records <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  # Decisions on title and abstract by a language model, one row for each record in each pass, committed with the protocol
  # The pilot pass read the author's 53 records blind under the first rule, the validation pass read 26 of them blind under the revised rule, and the screen pass read the rest
  model <- readr::read_csv("04.references/review/screening-model.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  # The author's decisions, entered by hand in the reading copy of review-records.csv that carries the abstracts, outside git
  # Excel opened that copy as Mac Roman, so the accented characters in its ids are converted back to UTF-8 before the join
  from_mac <- \(x) { y <- iconv(x, "UTF-8", "MACINTOSH"); Encoding(y) <- "UTF-8"; dplyr::coalesce(y, x) }
  by_hand <- readxl::read_excel("02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx", col_types = "text") |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = from_mac(id))
  stopifnot(setequal(by_hand$id, records$id), setequal(c(by_hand$id[!is.na(by_hand$decision)], model$id[model$pass == "screen"]), records$id))
  screening <- dplyr::select(by_hand, id, author = decision) |>
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::filter(model, pass %in% c("pilot", "screen")) |> dplyr::select(id, model = decision, reason, note), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(screener = dplyr::if_else(is.na(author), "model", "author"), decision = dplyr::coalesce(author, model), reason = dplyr::if_else(decision == "exclude", reason, NA)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, decision, reason, screener, author, note)
  readr::write_csv(screening, "02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv", na = "")
  wb <- openxlsx::loadWorkbook("02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx")
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, 1, dplyr::select(screening, decision, reason), startCol = 8)
  openxlsx::writeData(wb, 1, dplyr::select(screening, screener, note), startCol = 11)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, "02.inputs/review/raw/screening-with-abstracts.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
}
screening <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-screening.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: review-fulltext
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext.csv")) {
  squash <- \(x) stringr::str_remove_all(stringr::str_to_lower(stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "NFKC; Latin-ASCII")), "[^a-z0-9]")
  # library-science manifest, https://github.com/seamusrobertmurphy/library-science/blob/main/library/manifest.csv
  held_doi <- stringr::str_to_lower(stats::na.omit(readr::read_csv("../library-science/library/manifest.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)$doi))
  # PDFs saved by hand into library-science staging, named by author, year and title, outside git
  staged <- squash(stringr::str_remove(basename(list.files("../library-science/library/staging", "\\.pdf$", recursive = TRUE)), "^.*?\\b(19|20)[0-9]{2}\\b"))
  staged <- substr(staged[nchar(staged) >= 25], 1, 40)
  wanted <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-records.csv", col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::select(id, doi, title, year, routes, url) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(screening, decision %in% c("include", "undecided")) |> dplyr::select(id, decision), by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(work = squash(title),
                  held = dplyr::case_when(routes == "grey" ~ "04.references/literature", stringr::str_to_lower(doi) %in% held_doi ~ "library-science pdf",
                                          purrr::map_lgl(work, \(t) any(startsWith(t, staged))) ~ "library-science staging")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(.by = work, held = dplyr::first(held[!is.na(held)]), copy = dplyr::row_number() > 1)
  todo <- dplyr::filter(wanted, is.na(held), !copy)
  look_up <- function(doi, title) {
    req <- if (!is.na(doi)) {
      # OpenAlex work by DOI, a single-work lookup that costs nothing against the daily budget, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/get-a-single-work
      httr2::request(paste0("https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:", doi))
    } else {
      # OpenAlex works searched by title for a record with no DOI, at $0.001 of the $0.10 a day the unkeyed service allows, https://docs.openalex.org/api-entities/works/search-works
      httr2::request("https://api.openalex.org/works") |>
        httr2::req_url_query(filter = paste0("title.search:", stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(stringi::stri_trans_nfkc(title), "[^[:alnum:]]", " "))), `per-page` = 5)
    }
    w <- req |> httr2::req_url_query(select = "title,authorships,best_oa_location,locations") |> httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 4) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json()
    if (is.na(doi)) w <- purrr::detect(w$results, \(r) squash(r$title %||% "") == squash(title))
    list(urls = unique(stats::na.omit(c(w$best_oa_location$pdf_url %||% NA, purrr::map_chr(w$locations, \(l) l$pdf_url %||% NA)))),
         authors = purrr::map_chr(w$authorships, \(a) a$author$display_name %||% NA))
  }
  folder <- file.path("../library-science/library/staging", paste0("ipcc-uncertainties-", Sys.Date()))
  dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
  fetch <- function(id, doi, title, year, ...) {
    found <- look_up(doi, title)
    Sys.sleep(0.5)
    author <- stringr::word(found$authors[1], -1)
    name <- paste0(dplyr::coalesce(author, "Anon"), if (length(found$authors) > 2) " et al" else "", " ", year, " ",
                   stringr::str_trunc(stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(title, "[[:cntrl:]:/\\\\?*\"<>|]", " ")), 120, ellipsis = ""), ".pdf")
    if (file.exists(file.path(folder, name))) name <- sub("\\.pdf$", paste0(" ", substr(rlang::hash(id), 1, 6), ".pdf"), name)
    status <- "no open copy found"
    for (u in found$urls) {
      resp <- tryCatch(httr2::request(u) |> httr2::req_user_agent("ipcc-uncertainties literature review, R httr2") |> httr2::req_timeout(90) |>
                         httr2::req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |> httr2::req_perform(), error = \(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(resp)) { status <- "no answer from the open copy"; next }
      body <- if (httr2::resp_has_body(resp)) httr2::resp_body_raw(resp) else raw()
      if (httr2::resp_status(resp) == 200 && length(body) > 10000 && identical(body[1:4], charToRaw("%PDF"))) {
        writeBin(body, file.path(folder, name))
        return(tibble::tibble(id, author, status = "downloaded", pdf_url = u, file = name))
      }
      status <- if (httr2::resp_status(resp) == 200) "open copy is a web page, not a PDF" else paste("publisher refused,", httr2::resp_status(resp))
    }
    tibble::tibble(id, author, status, pdf_url = found$urls[1], file = NA_character_)
  }
  got <- purrr::pmap(dplyr::select(todo, id, doi, title, year), \(...) tryCatch(fetch(...), error = \(e) tibble::tibble(id = list(...)$id, author = NA_character_, status = paste("lookup failed,", conditionMessage(e)), pdf_url = NA_character_, file = NA_character_)), .progress = TRUE) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  log <- wanted |>
    dplyr::left_join(got, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::case_when(!is.na(held) ~ paste("held in", held), copy ~ "copy of a work listed above", .default = status)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, doi, author, title, year, decision, status, url, pdf_url, file)
  readr::write_csv(log, "02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext.csv", na = "")
  log |>
    dplyr::filter(!stringr::str_detect(status, "^(held|downloaded|copy)")) |>
    dplyr::transmute(author, year, title, decision, link = dplyr::coalesce(dplyr::if_else(is.na(doi), NA, paste0("https://doi.org/", doi)), url, pdf_url), status) |>
    readr::write_excel_csv("02.inputs/review/raw/pdfs-to-download.csv", na = "")
}
fulltext <- readr::read_csv("02.inputs/derived/review-fulltext.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: review-bib
#| echo: true

if (!file.exists("04.references/review/review.json")) {
  bib <- readr::read_file("04.references/references.bib")
  held <- tibble::tibble(key = stringr::str_match_all(bib, "@\\w+\\{([^,]+),[^@]*?doi\\s*=\\s*\\{([^}]+)\\}")[[1]][, 2], doi = stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_match_all(bib, "@\\w+\\{([^,]+),[^@]*?doi\\s*=\\s*\\{([^}]+)\\}")[[1]][, 3]))
  dois <- setdiff(stringr::str_to_lower(stats::na.omit(fulltext$doi[fulltext$status != "copy of a work listed above"])), held$doi)
  # CrossRef and DataCite records of each work, by DOI content negotiation, https://citation.crosscite.org/docs.html
  csl <- purrr::map(dois, \(d) tryCatch(httr2::request(paste0("https://doi.org/", d)) |> httr2::req_headers(Accept = "application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json") |> httr2::req_retry(max_tries = 3) |> httr2::req_perform() |> httr2::resp_body_json(), error = \(e) NULL), .progress = TRUE) |>
    purrr::compact() |>
    purrr::map(\(w) w[intersect(names(w), c("type", "title", "author", "editor", "issued", "container-title", "volume", "issue", "page", "DOI", "publisher", "URL"))])
  # CrossRef work types renamed to the item types of the Citation Style Language
  csl_type <- c(`journal-article` = "article-journal", `book-chapter` = "chapter", `posted-content` = "article", `proceedings-article` = "paper-conference", dissertation = "thesis", `peer-review` = "review", `reference-entry` = "entry", `report-component` = "report", monograph = "book", `edited-book` = "book")
  csl <- purrr::map(csl, \(w) purrr::list_modify(w, type = unname(dplyr::coalesce(csl_type[w$type], w$type))))
  # Names kept to their parts and titles to one string, the forms Pandoc reads from CSL JSON
  name_parts <- \(people) purrr::map(people, \(p) p[intersect(names(p), c("family", "given", "literal", "suffix", "non-dropping-particle", "dropping-particle"))]) |>
    purrr::keep(\(p) length(p[intersect(names(p), c("family", "given", "literal"))]) > 0)
  csl <- purrr::map(csl, \(w) {
    w$author <- if (length(w$author)) name_parts(w$author)
    w$editor <- if (length(w$editor)) name_parts(w$editor)
    when <- purrr::keep(w$issued$`date-parts`[[1]], is.numeric)
    w$issued <- if (length(when)) list(`date-parts` = list(when))
    w$title <- unlist(w$title)[1]
    w$`container-title` <- unlist(w$`container-title`)[1]
    w
  })
  minor <- c("from", "with", "what", "does", "into", "their", "this", "that", "under", "over", "using", "toward", "towards", "across", "between", "after", "about", "when", "where", "which")
  first_word <- \(t) purrr::detect(stringr::str_extract_all(stringr::str_to_lower(stringr::str_remove_all(paste(unlist(t), collapse = " "), "<[^>]+>")), "\\b[a-z]{4,}\\b")[[1]], \(w) !w %in% minor) %||% "work"
  key <- purrr::map_chr(csl, \(w) paste0(stringr::str_remove_all(stringi::stri_trans_general(stringr::str_to_lower(w$author[[1]]$family %||% w$author[[1]]$literal %||% w$publisher %||% "anon"), "Latin-ASCII"), "[^a-z]"),
                                         w$issued$`date-parts`[[1]][[1]] %||% "nd", first_word(w$title)))
  key <- stats::ave(key, key, FUN = \(k) if (length(k) == 1) k else paste0(k, letters[seq_along(k)]))
  stopifnot(!any(key %in% held$key))
  csl <- purrr::map2(csl, key, \(w, k) c(list(id = k), w))
  jsonlite::write_json(csl, "04.references/review/review.json", auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
  dplyr::bind_rows(held, tibble::tibble(key, doi = stringr::str_to_lower(purrr::map_chr(csl, "DOI")))) |>
    readr::write_csv("04.references/review/review-keys.csv")
}
```

```{r}
kappa <- \(a, b) {
  lv <- c("include", "exclude", "undecided")
  chance <- sum(prop.table(table(factor(a, lv))) * prop.table(table(factor(b, lv))))
  (mean(a == b) - chance) / (1 - chance)
}

  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(screening, id, author), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = pass, n = dplyr::n(), agree = sum(author == decision), kappa = kappa(author, decision))
```

On `r format(as.Date(min(search_log$date)), "%d %B %Y")` the `r nrow(oa)` searches of OpenAlex retrieved `r format(sum(oa$retrieved), big.mark = ",")` records on title and abstract, and the same searches of library-science, the author's store of sources verified against CrossRef, retrieved `r sum(search_log$retrieved[search_log$strand == "library-science"])`. `r if (all(!is.na(s2$error))) "Semantic Scholar refused every search made without an access key, so it contributed no records." else paste0("Semantic Scholar retrieved ", format(sum(s2$retrieved), big.mark = ","), " records.")` Merging records that shared a DOI or a title, and adding `r sum(records$routes == "grey")` guidelines, standards, inventory reports and methodological notes sought by hand from the IPCC, Environment and Climate Change Canada, Architecture for REDD+ Transactions and FAO, left `r format(nrow(records), big.mark = ",")` unique records to screen. Scopus and Web of Science were not searched, because both required an institutional key.

The author screened the first `r sum(records$screener == "author")` records on title and abstract, including a record that mentioned natural, anthropogenic, human-induced or any other kind of disturbance. His decisions showed that a record was excluded when disturbance was only background to another subject. The remaining `r format(sum(records$screener == "model"), big.mark = ",")` records were screened against a written form of that rule by a large language model (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic), given his decisions as worked examples. Tried blind on `r validation$n` of his records, with the other `r sum(records$screener == "author") - validation$n` as examples, the model agreed with him on `r validation$agree` [Cohen's κ = `r sprintf("%.2f", validation$kappa)`]. Of the `r format(nrow(records), big.mark = ",")` records, `r sum(records$decision == "include")` were included and `r sum(records$decision == "exclude")` excluded, `r sum(records$reason == "wrong-concept", na.rm = TRUE)` of them because they concerned forest or land but none of the review's concepts, and `r sum(records$decision == "undecided")` were left undecided for want of an abstract. Open copies of the included and undecided works were sought through OpenAlex, and `r sum(stringr::str_detect(works$status, "^(held|downloaded)"))` of the `r nrow(works)` works were already in the library or were downloaded.

The same model then charted each of the `r format(nrow(charting), big.mark = ",")` distinct included and undecided works from its title and abstract under a written rule. Each chart recorded the review questions the work bore on, its place, scale, method and disturbance, its finding, and a passage of its abstract, copied word for word, that a script checked against the abstract. The `r sum(charting$basis == "title")` works with no abstract were charted from their titles alone. The charted works bore on the effect of the separation on reported emissions in `r on("q1")` cases, the statistics of disturbance regimes in `r on("q2")`, the uncertainty of carbon flux estimates in `r on("q3")`, fire emission data in `r on("q4")` and crediting or reversal in `r on("q5")`, and `r sum(charting$role == "central")` bore directly on this study. The full texts were not read for the charting, so any statement that the charted works lacked a kind of study rests on titles and abstracts.

## Data sources

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sources
#| tbl-cap: "Datasets this study read, with the release used and what each one supplies."
#| echo: true

sources <- data.frame(
  Dataset = c("FAOSTAT Emissions from Fires (GI)",
              "FAO AllFires_OrganicSoils table",
              "MODIS MCD64A1 Collection 6.1",
              "MODIS MCD12Q1 Collection 6.1"),
  Publisher = c("FAO", "FAO", "NASA", "NASA"),
  Supplies = c("Burned area, burned biomass and emissions by country and year",
               "Organic soil fire values set to zero in the published domain",
               "Monthly burned area at 500 m, the input FAOSTAT aggregates",
               "Annual land cover at 500 m, the vegetation strata FAOSTAT applies"),
  Period = c("1990-2024", "1990-2021", "2000-2024", "2001-2023"))
readr::write_csv(sources, "03.outputs/TBL/tbl-sources.csv")
fmt_tbl(sources)
```

## Fire emissions from FAOSTAT

FAOSTAT computed the fire emissions of each pixel as its burned area multiplied by the fuel consumption of its vegetation type and by the default emission factor of each gas [@fao2025fires]. It summed them to countries with the FAO Global Administrative Unit Layers and published them for forest fires, savanna fires and fires in organic soils. Its methodological note stated that forest fire carbon dioxide was left out because the FAOSTAT Forests domain counted it, and that savanna fire carbon dioxide was left out on the assumption that regrowth balanced it within a year [@fao2025fires]. The domain nonetheless returned carbon dioxide for forest fires from 2001, and those values are reported here. Each year's value was compared with the value Canada submitted for the same item, which FAOSTAT published in the same domain, following comparisons of FAOSTAT with national inventories [@grassi2022carbon; @nyawira2024pantropical] and of an independent model with European inventories [@pilli2016modellinga]. The coefficients FAOSTAT applied were then recovered from its published values for Canada. Biomass burned divided by burned area gave the fuel consumed per hectare, and each emission divided by biomass burned gave the emission factor per kilogram of dry matter, both compared with Tables 2.4 and 2.5 of the 2006 Guidelines that the note cited [@aalde2006generic; @fao2025fires].

The domain was retrieved through the FAOSTAT application programming interface, which required an account. The analysis chunk authenticated with credentials stored in the environment, requested the domain for Canada and cached the response for later renders.


## Fires in organic soils

The values FAO withheld from the domain were read from its `AllFires_OrganicSoils` table, released as a related document of the domain. The analysis chunk kept only lines containing a complete record, so that a line broken across a page could not enter as a partial one, and checked that every combination of area, year and element appeared once.


## The natural disturbance rule

Australia's rule was applied to the Canadian series in the form its inventory used, a year counting as natural when its fire emissions exceeded the baseline mean by two standard deviations [@bowman2023wildfire]. The rule was run on baselines of 13, 20 and 30 years, the first being the length Australia used, 2000 to 2012.


## Canada's reported components

Canada's disaggregated series was taken from Table 6-1 of the 2026 national inventory report, which Environment and Climate Change Canada published for each year from 1990 to 2024 and for each province and territory [@eccc2026nir]. The table gave the net emissions of the land use sector, the account Canada reported, and on a separate line the net emissions of land affected by natural disturbance, which Canada tracked but left out of its total. Both lines were read for Canada and British Columbia, and both came from Canada's National Forest Carbon Monitoring, Accounting and Reporting System. Its core model, CBM-CFS3, grew each stand along an empirical yield curve and moved its carbon through a disturbance matrix for each type of disturbance [@kurz2018quantifying], and its fire matrices assumed that every fire burned at high severity [@thompson2026incorporating]. British Columbia's share of the area burned in Canada each year was computed from the Canadian National Fire Database, which contained the fire polygons of every provincial, territorial and federal agency. The two accounts were compared over 1990 to 2024 by the mean and standard deviation of their annual net emissions, following @kurz2024revised, before the crediting arithmetic was applied to the years from 2012.


## Crediting under the standard

The two deductions were implemented as the standard wrote them, so that the share of gross reductions and removals a jurisdiction kept could be read at any uncertainty. The uncertainty deduction took the adjustment factor of the standard's Equation 11, and the buffer took the contribution of its Table 2 [@art2021trees].


The uncertainty of each account came from the published uncertainty of the model behind Canada's estimates, a 95 per cent interval 32.2 Tg C a year wide [@metsaranta2017uncertainty]. It was applied as a standard deviation to every annual flux in both accounts, which assumed the model was no more certain of a megafire year than of a quiet one. The crediting level was the mean emissions of the five-year reference period, 2012 to 2016, and the reduction in each crediting year, 2017 to 2024, was that level minus the emissions reported for the year [@art2021trees]. Both were computed on the human activity component alone, the disaggregated account Canada reported, and on the sum of the two components, the account without disaggregation.


# Results

## Reported national emissions

```{r}
#| label: fig-accounts
#| fig-cap: "Net emissions of the land use sector for Canada and British Columbia, 1990 to 2024, in the account Canada reports, with natural disturbance separated, and in the undisaggregated account, the reported total plus the natural disturbance component. Positive values are emissions and negative values are removals."
#| echo: true

eccc |>
  dplyr::mutate(region = factor(dplyr::if_else(region == "BC", "British Columbia", region), levels = c("Canada", "British Columbia"))) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(human, net), names_to = "account", values_to = "mt") |>
  dplyr::mutate(account = dplyr::if_else(account == "human", "Disaggregated, as reported", "Undisaggregated")) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(year, mt, linetype = account)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~region, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = expression("Net emissions (Mt CO"[2]*"e)"), linetype = NULL) +
  th +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Separating natural disturbance cut the standard deviation of Canada's annual land use emissions from `r round(stats::sd(national$net))` to `r round(stats::sd(national$human))` Mt CO~2~e over 1990 to 2024, a factor of `r round(stats::sd(national$net) / stats::sd(national$human), 1)` (@fig-accounts). The account Canada reported averaged `r msd(national$human)`, against `r msd(national$net)` without the separation. The difference, the natural disturbance component, ran from `r round(min(national$natural))` Mt in `r national$year[which.min(national$natural)]` to `r format(round(max(national$natural)), big.mark = ",")` Mt in `r national$year[which.max(national$natural)]`, and in 2023 Canada reported `r national$human[national$year == 2023]` Mt where the undisaggregated account showed `r format(round(national$net[national$year == 2023]), big.mark = ",")` Mt. British Columbia's reported account averaged `r msd(province$human)` against `r msd(province$net)` without the separation, a standard deviation `r round(stats::sd(province$net) / stats::sd(province$human), 1)` times larger, and in 2023 the province reported `r province$human[province$year == 2023]` Mt against `r round(province$net[province$year == 2023])` Mt.
